Tutorial: from data to evaluation

Follow OpenCabinet from a fresh checkout to replay checks, image inputs, training and a reproducible checkpoint evaluation.

One stage, the whole pipeline

This walkthrough uses OpenCabinet, the first stage of Cabinet & Pouring: CabinetPouringOpenCabinet-Sharpa-v1, the left Franka arm with a Sharpa hand, a registered 600-step horizon and 100 released demonstration episodes. It is one stage, not the complete cabinet sequence.

  1. Install the public runtime and meshes
  2. Download and validate a stage dataset
  3. Render fixed policy inputs
  4. Train ACT or choose a released checkpoint
  5. Evaluate, preserve episode records and compare the declared protocol
Keep functional checks separate from benchmark results

Short runs and the maintainers' November release-validation observations help check an installation. They do not update the manuscript Leaderboard. The public code has evolved since the paper; report the exact source, checkpoint and evaluation settings.

1. Install and authenticate

Follow Installation, including the RTX 50-series wheel adjustment if needed. Request access on the dataset page ↗ before running:

git clone https://github.com/SIPAIR-Elastic/DexArena.git
cd DexArena
conda create -n ms3 python=3.10
conda activate ms3
python -m pip install datasets "lerobot==0.4.0"
python -m pip install --upgrade mani_skill "gymnasium==0.29.1" tyro swanlab h5py tensorboard coacd
hf auth login
hf download SIPAIR/DexArena --repo-type dataset --include "assets/**" --local-dir tasks
python -m pip install pytest
python -m pytest tests -q

2. Get the data and resolve task metadata

Keep the following shell variables in the same terminal for the later steps:

DEX_ENV=CabinetPouringOpenCabinet-Sharpa-v1
DEX_ROBOT=panda_sharpa_hand_left_angled_mobile_base
hf download SIPAIR/DexArena --repo-type dataset --include "data/sharpa/$DEX_ENV/**" --local-dir .
python -c "from utils.dex_tasks import resolve_dex_task; t=resolve_dex_task('$DEX_ENV'); print(t.robot_uids, t.max_episode_steps)"

Inspect the downloaded Parquet files in Python. Shell variables are not Python local variables, so define the task name explicitly:

from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd

env_id = "CabinetPouringOpenCabinet-Sharpa-v1"
files = sorted(Path("data/sharpa", env_id, "data/chunk-000").glob("*.parquet"))
df = pd.concat((pd.read_parquet(path) for path in files), ignore_index=True)
print(len(df), df["episode_index"].nunique())  # release snapshot: 13121, 100

3. Check restoration and replay

python -m data_gen.replay.verify_recording_fidelity --episodes 2 --action-replay data/sharpa/$DEX_ENV
python -m data_gen.replay.replay_success_rate --jobs 3 --json-out replay.json data/sharpa/$DEX_ENV

Look for a faithful restoration result and a complete replay denominator. The maintainers' reference run reached success on 100/100 episodes; 98/100 remained successful at the final step. Your report should retain its own output and source fingerprint. See the two validation contracts.

4. Render image-policy inputs

python -m data_gen.render_pixel_demos --demo-path data/sharpa/$DEX_ENV --env-id $DEX_ENV \
  --robot-uids $DEX_ROBOT --control-mode pd_joint_pos \
  --camera-preset cabinet_fixed --image-size 256 --max-episode-steps 600 \
  --out data/pixels/"$DEX_ENV"_256.h5
python train/prepare_image_dataset.py --pixels data/pixels/"$DEX_ENV"_256.h5 --out data/act/$DEX_ENV

The converted dataset contains state/action arrays, six image arrays (two cameras × history offsets 0, 2, 4), episode metadata and dataset_info.json. Inspect the renderer's first episode before training. This reconstructs recorded frames; it is not a new simulation rollout.

5. Train ACT

This copyable example defines its camera and environment flags on the page. It runs 20,000 updates on the released stage data; GPU time and memory depend on your machine. Bash arrays keep every flag separate.

DEX_CAMS=(
  --camera-names base_camera_t0 base_camera_tm2 base_camera_tm4 task_wrist_camera_t0 task_wrist_camera_tm2 task_wrist_camera_tm4
  --camera-map base_camera_t0=base_camera base_camera_tm2=base_camera base_camera_tm4=base_camera task_wrist_camera_t0=task_wrist_camera task_wrist_camera_tm2=task_wrist_camera task_wrist_camera_tm4=task_wrist_camera
  --camera-history-offsets base_camera_t0=0 base_camera_tm2=2 base_camera_tm4=4 task_wrist_camera_t0=0 task_wrist_camera_tm2=2 task_wrist_camera_tm4=4
)
DEX_ENVFLAGS=(
  --env-id "$DEX_ENV" --task-module tasks --robot-uids "$DEX_ROBOT" --control-mode pd_joint_pos
  --obs-mode rgb --env-kwarg show_guidance_markers=false --sim-backend physx_cpu
  --camera-preset cabinet_fixed --image-size 256
  --policy-state-mode paths --online-state-paths agent.qpos --expected-raw-state-dim 29 --expected-policy-state-dim 29
)
python train/train_ACT.py --demo-data-path data/act/$DEX_ENV "${DEX_ENVFLAGS[@]}" "${DEX_CAMS[@]}" \
  --validation-ratio 0.1 --image-mean 0.485 0.456 0.406 --image-std 0.229 0.224 0.225 \
  --image-encoder-backbone resnet18 --image-encoder-pretrained --chunk-size 25 --prior-l1-weight 1.0 \
  --action-loss-groups 0:7 7:29 --action-loss-group-weights 2.0 1.0 \
  --batch-size 16 --num-workers 4 --steps 20000 --eval-every 1000 --save-every 1000 --num-eval-episodes 0 \
  --output-dir runs/act --exp-name "$DEX_ENV"_s1 --seed 1

For Diffusion Policy, PPO, RLPD, GR00T or π0.5, use the method-specific recipes and runtimes in Training. The tutorial does not start a long-running training process for you.

6. Evaluate a released checkpoint

You can skip training and evaluate the released ACT policy. This example uses the registered 600-step horizon and 50 episodes; it is not the draft's shorter 400-step functional recipe. Resolve the horizon again if you switch tasks.

hf download SIPAIR/DexArena --repo-type dataset --local-dir . --include "ckpt/act/$DEX_ENV/**"
python train/train_ACT.py --evaluate --checkpoint ckpt/act/$DEX_ENV/ckpt.pt \
  --env-id $DEX_ENV --task-module tasks --robot-uids $DEX_ROBOT --control-mode pd_joint_pos \
  --obs-mode rgb --env-kwarg show_guidance_markers=false --sim-backend physx_cpu \
  --camera-preset cabinet_fixed --image-size 256 \
  --num-eval-episodes 50 --num-eval-steps 600 --eval-seed 1 --eval-reconfiguration-freq 0 \
  --capture-video --max-eval-videos 3

Inspect the per-episode [EVAL] lines, final JSON summary, videos and the CSV under ckpt/act/$DEX_ENV/eval_logs_eval_only/. To test your training run, replace --checkpoint with a checkpoint file under runs/act/.

7. Read and report the result

One task's success rate is not the method's benchmark average. Stage execution averages the 30 stage rates; cross-scene evaluation repeats a frozen policy on the three named kitchens; long-horizon evaluation attempts all stages of a complete sequence after one reset.

The released ACT manifest reports 47/50 on OpenCabinet. That is a checkpoint-release record, not a promise that a changed code revision, seed list or horizon will reproduce the same count. The manuscript scores on the Leaderboard remain a distinct fixed snapshot.

Follow what to report with a number: code and data revisions, checkpoint hash, environment, embodiment, camera preprocessing, horizon, seeds, instruction rule, scene and per-episode records.

8. Continue the experiment

  • Another task: resolve its robot, horizon and inputs using Task metadata ↗ and the task table ↗.
  • Another hand: inspect -Wuji-v1, -XHand-v1 and -Gripper-v1; published demonstrations and checkpoints are Sharpa-only.
  • Scene transfer or complete sequences: follow Evaluation and Long-horizon guide ↗.
  • Sharing a result: preserve reproduction artifacts and include the citation.
